# Overview

Behavioural analysis of the monetary incentive delay (MID) task in a
within-subject, placebo-controlled study with three sessions:
methylphenidate (MPH), sulpiride (SUL) and placebo (PBO). This document:

1. Builds the per-subject summary matrix from the trial-level data
   (`trialwiseMID.csv`) and excludes outlying sessions (|z(RT)| > 3).
2. Runs 2 x 3 repeated-measures ANOVAs (Reward x Drug) on RT, hit,
   too-late and too-early rates, with Holm-corrected pairwise drug
   contrasts. (Miss = 1 - hit, so its ANOVA would duplicate the hit ANOVA.)
3. Tests whether baseline dopamine synthesis capacity (ki, [18F]-FDOPA PET)
   moderates the drug or reward effects (mixed ANCOVA).
4. Fits ex-Gaussian RT distributions per subject and tests drug and reward
   effects on mu, sigma and tau.
5. Writes per-subject behavioural drug effects used as covariates in the
   fMRI group models (`MID_beh_covariates.csv`).
6. Builds the publication tables of the fMRI cluster results.

**Response coding** (`resp` column): `1` = hit, `2` = too late, `-1` = too early,
`0` = no response. `miss` = every non-hit trial (`resp != 1`), i.e. miss =
early + late + no-response.

# Configuration & packages

```{r config}
## --- Paths -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional local copy of the data (same relative layout as the project
# folder), set via the MID_LOCAL_DATA environment variable; otherwise the
# project storage is used.
localCandidates <- Sys.getenv("MID_LOCAL_DATA")
localHit <- localCandidates[nzchar(localCandidates) & dir.exists(localCandidates)]

if (length(localHit) > 0) {
  projectDir <- localHit[1]
} else if (Sys.info()["sysname"] == "Windows") {
  projectDir <- "P:/3017048.01"
} else {
  projectDir <- "/project/3017048.01"
}
behDir <- file.path(projectDir, "bids", "derivatives", "beh", "MID", "stats")

trial_file <- file.path(behDir, "trialwiseMID.csv")

outDir <- file.path(behDir, "MID_output")
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = FALSE)

## Save a ggplot/ggarrange figure as both .png and .pdf
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(outDir, paste0(name, ".png")), plot,
                   width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(outDir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), plot,
                   width = width, height = height)
}
## --- Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
packages <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "ggplot2", "afex", "emmeans",
              "rstatix", "ggpubr", "tibble", "ggrain", "sjPlot", "effectsize",
              'kableExtra')

to_install <- setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install)
invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE))

afex::afex_options(es_aov = "pes", correction_aov = "GG",
                   emmeans_model = "multivariate")

nTrialsTotal <- 56   # trials per session
nTrialsCell  <- 28   # trials per reward per session

## Drug colours (colour-blind safe)
drug_cols <- c(PBO = "#F0E442", MPH = "#009E73", SUL = "#56B4E9")
```

# Load trial-wise data

`trialwiseMID.csv` has no header. Columns: subject, session, trial, drug,
5 ki values (striatal ROIs), resp, rt (target-locked), reward type, rtCue
(cue-locked) and trial-timing columns.

```{r load}
raw <- readr::read_csv(trial_file, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE)

trial <- raw %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    subject = X1,
    session = X2,
    trial   = X3,
    drug    = factor(X4, levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                     labels = c("PBO", "MPH", "SUL")),
    resp    = X10,                       # 1 hit, 2 late, -1 early, 0 no-resp
    rt      = X11,                       # target-locked RT (hits + lates only)
    reward  = factor(X12, levels = c(1, 2),
                     labels = c("Low", "High")),
    rtCue   = X13                        # cue-locked response time
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(reward))                 # drop trials with no reward code

## ki values (one row per subject, constant within subject)
ki <- raw %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject = X1) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(strki = dplyr::first(X5), putki = dplyr::first(X6), caudki = dplyr::first(X7),
            dcaudki = dplyr::first(X8), vstrki = dplyr::first(X9), .groups = "drop")
```

# Build the per-subject summary matrix

Response rates and mean RT per subject x drug x reward cell, and per
subject x drug.

```{r summary-matrix}
## Cell level: subject x drug x reward.
## Denominator = actual trial count in the cell (n_cell), not a fixed 28.
cell <- trial %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject, drug, reward) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_cell = n(),                                   # trials in this cell
    hit    = sum(resp == 1,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_cell,
    late   = sum(resp == 2,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_cell,
    early  = sum(resp == -1, na.rm = TRUE) / n_cell,
    nr     = sum(resp == 0,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_cell,
    miss   = sum(resp != 1,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_cell,
    ## RT averaged over hits + lates only
    rt     = mean(rt[resp == 1 | resp == 2], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Report any cell short of the intended 28 trials
short_cells <- cell %>% dplyr::filter(n_cell != nTrialsCell)
if (nrow(short_cells) > 0) {
  message(nrow(short_cells), " cell(s) do not have ", nTrialsCell,
          " trials (rates still correct via per-cell denominator):")
  print(short_cells %>% dplyr::select(subject, drug, reward, n_cell))
}

## Drug level: collapsed across reward.
## Denominator = actual trial count in the session (n_sess), not a fixed 56.
drug_lvl <- trial %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject, drug) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_sess = n(),
    hit    = sum(resp == 1,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_sess,
    late   = sum(resp == 2,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_sess,
    early  = sum(resp == -1, na.rm = TRUE) / n_sess,
    nr     = sum(resp == 0,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_sess,
    miss   = sum(resp != 1,  na.rm = TRUE) / n_sess,
    rt     = mean(rt[resp == 1 | resp == 2], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Long format used by every ANOVA below
beh_long_all <- cell %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subject = factor(subject))

## Wide summary matrix, one row per subject
beh_wide_all <- cell %>%
  dplyr::select(-n_cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = c(reward, drug),
    values_from = c(rt, hit, late, early, miss, nr),
    names_glue  = "{.value}{reward}{drug}"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    drug_lvl %>%
      dplyr::select(-n_sess) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = drug,
                  values_from = c(rt, hit, late, early, miss, nr),
                  names_glue = "{.value}{drug}"),
    by = "subject"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ki, by = "subject")

readr::write_csv(beh_wide_all, file.path(outDir, "MID_summary_matrix.csv"))
head(beh_long_all)
```
# Session-level outlier exclusion (RT)

Mean RT is computed per subject x session. Sessions without any hit or
late response are missing data, not outliers, and are left out of the
z-scoring. RTs of the remaining sessions are z-scored against the grand
mean and SD across all sessions, and a session is excluded if
|z(RT)| > 3. The excluded sessions are removed from every analysis below
(and from the fMRI group models).

```{r outlier-exclusion-session}
criterion <- 3  # SD threshold

## ---- 1. Per-session RT (hits + lates) -------------------------------------
session_means <- trial %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject, session) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    rt_sess  = mean(rt[resp %in% c(1, 2)], na.rm = TRUE),
    acc_sess = sum(resp == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / nTrialsTotal,
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(incomplete = is.nan(rt_sess))  # no hit/late trials at all -> no RT to average

## ---- 2. Grand-mean z on RT, complete sessions only -----------------------
complete <- session_means %>% dplyr::filter(!incomplete)

mu_rt <- mean(complete$rt_sess, na.rm = T)
sd_rt <- sd(complete$rt_sess, na.rm = T)

session_means <- session_means %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z_rt    = (rt_sess - mu_rt) / sd_rt,
    outlier = !incomplete & !is.na(z_rt) & abs(z_rt) > criterion
  )

## ---- 3. Report -----------------------------------------------------------
flagged <- session_means %>% dplyr::filter(outlier)

cat(sprintf("Grand RT mean = %.3f s, SD = %.3f\n", mu_rt, sd_rt))
cat(sprintf("Complete sessions: %d / %d (incomplete: %d)\n\n",
            nrow(complete), nrow(session_means),
            sum(session_means$incomplete)))
cat(sprintf("Flagged sessions (|z(RT)| > %d): %d, in %d subjects\n\n",
            criterion, nrow(flagged), dplyr::n_distinct(flagged$subject)))

print(flagged %>% dplyr::select(subject, session, rt_sess, z_rt, acc_sess),
      n = Inf)

readr::write_csv(session_means,
                 file.path(outDir, "MID_session_outlier_flags.csv"))

## ---- 4. Map (subject, session) -> drug; drop from beh_long ---------------
if (!exists("drugcodes")) {
  drugcodes_file <- file.path(projectDir, "admin", "9.Deblinding",
                              "drugcodes_sessByDrug.csv")
  drugcodes <- readr::read_csv(drugcodes_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

drug_long <- drugcodes %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(MPHsession, SULsession, PBOsession),
                      names_to = "drug", values_to = "session") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(drug = sub("session$", "", drug))

flagged_drug <- flagged %>%
  dplyr::select(subject, session) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(drug_long, by = c("subject", "session"))

cat("\nFlagged sessions mapped to drug:\n")
print(flagged_drug, n = Inf)

## (subject, drug) cells to remove: the RT-outlier sessions. Incomplete
## sessions are not added here; they were only left out of the z-scoring.
to_remove <- flagged_drug

cat(sprintf("\nTotal cells to remove from beh_long: %d (%d outlier)\n",
            nrow(to_remove), nrow(flagged_drug)))

## Remove the to_remove (subject, drug) cells from any data frame with
## subject + drug columns, so every analysis below (ANOVAs, ex-Gaussian
## fits, response-time profiles) uses the same exclusions.
drop_flagged_cells <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(subject_chr = as.character(subject)) %>%
    dplyr::anti_join(
      to_remove %>% dplyr::mutate(subject_chr = as.character(subject)) %>%
        dplyr::select(subject_chr, drug),
      by = c("subject_chr", "drug")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-subject_chr)
}

beh_long <- beh_long_all %>% drop_flagged_cells() %>% droplevels()

cat(sprintf("\nbeh_long after exclusion: %d unique subjects, %d rows\n",
            dplyr::n_distinct(beh_long$subject), nrow(beh_long)))

## Same exclusion on the trial-level data (ex-Gaussian fits, RT profiles)
trial_excl <- trial %>% drop_flagged_cells() %>% droplevels()

cat(sprintf("trial_excl after exclusion: %d unique subjects, %d rows (from %d)\n",
            dplyr::n_distinct(trial_excl$subject), nrow(trial_excl), nrow(trial)))
```

# ANOVA helper

`afex::aov_ez` runs the 2 x 3 repeated-measures ANOVA, applies
Greenhouse-Geisser correction when sphericity is violated, and reports partial
eta-squared. Subjects with any missing cell are dropped listwise (required for a
within-subjects ANOVA).

```{r anova-fn}
run_rm_anova <- function(data, dv, dv_label = dv) {
  d <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(subject, drug, reward, all_of(dv)) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  keep <- d %>% dplyr::count(subject) %>% dplyr::filter(n == 6) %>% dplyr::pull(subject)
  d <- d %>% dplyr::filter(subject %in% keep) %>% droplevels()

  aov_res <- afex::aov_ez(id = "subject", dv = dv, data = d,
                          within = c("drug", "reward"))
  cat("\n### ANOVA:", dv_label, "  (N =", nlevels(d$subject), ")\n")
  print(aov_res)

  ## pairwise drug contrasts (Holm-corrected)
  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(aov_res, ~ drug)
  cat("\nPairwise drug contrasts:\n")
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "holm"))

  invisible(list(anova = aov_res, emm = emm, data = d))
}
```

# Combined results table

```{r results-table}
tidy_anova <- function(res, dv_label) {
  res$anova$anova_table %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Effect") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(DV = dv_label, .before = 1)
}

all_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidy_anova(res_rt,    "Reaction time"),
  tidy_anova(res_hit,   "Hit rate"),
  tidy_anova(res_late,  "Too-late rate"),
  tidy_anova(res_early, "Too-early rate")
)
print(all_results, digits = 3)
readr::write_csv(all_results, file.path(outDir, "MID_ANOVA_results.csv"))
```

# Publication table

A formatted ANOVA table for the manuscript: F, degrees of freedom
(Greenhouse-Geisser corrected where sphericity was violated), p-value, and
partial eta-squared as the effect size. `sjPlot::tab_df` renders an HTML table
that can be copied straight into a manuscript or saved to file.

```{r pub-table}
## ---- ANOVA rows: one row per effect, F(df1,df2) + p + partial eta^2 -------
## afex anova_table columns: "num Df", "den Df", "MSE", "F", "pes", "Pr(>F)".
anova_rows <- function(res) {
  at <- as.data.frame(res$anova$anova_table)
  data.frame(
    Effect = c("Drug", "Reward", "Drug x Reward"),
    Statistic = sprintf("%.2f (%.0f, %.0f)",
                        at[["F"]], at[["num Df"]], at[["den Df"]]),
    p = ifelse(at[["Pr(>F)"]] < .001, "< .001",
               sprintf("%.3f", at[["Pr(>F)"]])),
    ES = sprintf("%.3f", at[["pes"]]),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  )
}

## ---- Pairwise drug contrast rows: one row per contrast --------------------
## emmeans pairs() gives estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value (Holm-adjusted).
## Effect size = Cohen's d for paired data, d = t / sqrt(n), with n = df + 1.
contrast_rows <- function(res) {
  ct <- as.data.frame(pairs(res$emm, adjust = "holm"))
  d  <- ct$t.ratio / sqrt(ct$df + 1)
  data.frame(
    Effect = as.character(ct$contrast),
    Statistic = sprintf("t(%.0f) = %.2f", ct$df, ct$t.ratio),
    p = ifelse(ct$p.value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", ct$p.value)),
    ES = sprintf("%.2f", d),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  )
}

dvs <- list("Reaction time" = res_rt,  "Hit rate"       = res_hit,
            "Too-late rate" = res_late, "Too-early rate" = res_early)

## ---- Stack ANOVA section then contrast section ----------------------------
## Strip row names so rbind does not append .1/.2/.3 suffixes.
anova_block    <- do.call(rbind, lapply(dvs, anova_rows))
contrast_block <- do.call(rbind, lapply(dvs, contrast_rows))
rownames(anova_block)    <- NULL
rownames(contrast_block) <- NULL
tbl <- rbind(anova_block, contrast_block)
rownames(tbl) <- NULL

## row counts per DV (3 effects each in ANOVA; 3 pairs each in contrasts)
n_aov <- vapply(dvs, function(r) nrow(anova_rows(r)),    integer(1))
n_con <- vapply(dvs, function(r) nrow(contrast_rows(r)), integer(1))

## ---- Build the kable ------------------------------------------------------
## Generic column headers (Statistic / Effect size) because the two sections
## report different quantities - explained in the footnote.
table_beh <- tbl %>%
  kable("html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
        caption = 'Table 1. Repeated-measures ANOVA of MID behaviour (Drug x Reward) and pairwise drug contrasts',
        col.names = c(" ", "Statistic", "<i>P</i>", "Effect size")) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = "Cambria",
                font_size = 16, position = 'center') %>%
  pack_rows("Omnibus ANOVA", 1, nrow(anova_block)) %>%
  pack_rows("Pairwise drug contrasts (Holm-corrected)",
            nrow(anova_block) + 1, nrow(tbl))

## per-DV italic sub-headers within each section
start <- 0
for (i in seq_along(dvs)) {
  table_beh <- table_beh %>%
    pack_rows(names(dvs)[i], start + 1, start + n_aov[i],
              label_row_css = "font-style: italic;")
  start <- start + n_aov[i]
}
for (i in seq_along(dvs)) {
  table_beh <- table_beh %>%
    pack_rows(names(dvs)[i], start + 1, start + n_con[i],
              label_row_css = "font-style: italic;")
  start <- start + n_con[i]
}

table_beh <- table_beh %>%
  footnote(general = paste(
    "Omnibus ANOVA rows: Statistic is F (df1, df2), Effect size is partial eta-squared;",
    "Greenhouse-Geisser correction applied where sphericity was violated.",
    "Contrast rows: Statistic is t (df), Effect size is Cohen's d for paired data (d = t / sqrt(n));",
    "paired t-tests with Holm correction for multiple comparisons."),
    general_title = "Note. ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)

table_beh

## ---- Save -----------------------------------------------------------------
readr::write_csv(tbl, file.path(outDir, "MID_behaviour_table.csv"))

if (!requireNamespace("webshot2", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("webshot2")
kableExtra::save_kable(table_beh,
                       file = file.path(outDir, "MID_behaviour_table.png"), zoom = 2)
kableExtra::save_kable(table_beh,
                       file = file.path(outDir, "MID_behaviour_table.pdf"))
```
# Baseline dopamine synthesis capacity (ki) as a moderator
```{r ki-covariate-anova}
## ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Does the Drug or Reward effect depend on baseline dopamine synthesis (ki)?
##
## ki is constant within subject => a BETWEEN-subjects covariate.
## Model: mixed ANCOVA with within factors Drug, Reward and continuous
## covariate ki. The terms of interest are the ki interactions:
##   Drug:ki, Reward:ki, Drug:Reward:ki
## A non-significant interaction => the effect does not depend on baseline DA.
## afex::aov_ez takes the covariate via `covariate=` with `factorize=FALSE`.
## ki is mean-centred so the main effects remain interpretable.
## ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ki ROIs to test: whole striatum, caudate, putamen, ventral striatum
ki_rois <- c(strki  = "Whole striatum",
             caudki = "Caudate",
             putki  = "Putamen",
             vstrki = "Ventral striatum")

## Behavioural DVs to test
ki_dvs <- c(rt = "Reaction time", hit = "Hit rate",
            late = "Too-late rate", early = "Too-early rate")

## One mixed ANCOVA: dv ~ drug * reward * ki, for one DV and one ROI.
run_ki_anova <- function(data, dv, roi_col) {

d <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(subject = as.character(subject)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      ki %>% dplyr::mutate(subject = as.character(subject)) %>%
             dplyr::select(subject, kicov = all_of(roi_col)),
      by = "subject"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(subject, drug, reward, kicov, val = all_of(dv)) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()

  ## keep only subjects with all 6 within-cells AND a ki value
  keep <- d %>% dplyr::count(subject) %>%
    dplyr::filter(n == 6) %>% dplyr::pull(subject)
  d <- d %>% dplyr::filter(subject %in% keep) %>% droplevels()

  ## mean-centre the covariate
  d$kicov <- d$kicov - mean(d$kicov)

  afex::aov_ez(id = "subject", dv = "val", data = d,
               within = c("drug", "reward"),
               covariate = "kicov", factorize = FALSE)
}

## Extract the three ki-interaction rows from an aov_ez object.
ki_interaction_rows <- function(aov_res, dv_label, roi_label) {
  at <- as.data.frame(aov_res$anova_table)
  at$Term <- rownames(at)
wanted <- c("kicov:drug", "kicov:reward", "kicov:drug:reward")
  pretty <- c("kicov:drug"        = "Drug \u00D7 ki",
              "kicov:reward"      = "Reward \u00D7 ki",
              "kicov:drug:reward" = "Drug \u00D7 Reward \u00D7 ki")
  out <- at[at$Term %in% wanted, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    DV        = dv_label,
    ROI       = roi_label,
    Effect    = pretty[out$Term],
    Statistic = sprintf("%.2f (%.0f, %.0f)",
                        out[["F"]], out[["num Df"]], out[["den Df"]]),
    p         = ifelse(out[["Pr(>F)"]] < .001, "< .001",
                       sprintf("%.3f", out[["Pr(>F)"]])),
    ES        = sprintf("%.3f", out[["pes"]]),
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE
  )
}

## Run across all DV x ROI combinations
ki_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(ki_dvs), function(dv) {
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      lapply(names(ki_rois), function(roi) {
        aov_res <- run_ki_anova(beh_long, dv, roi)
        ki_interaction_rows(aov_res, ki_dvs[[dv]], ki_rois[[roi]])
      })
    )
  })
)

print(ki_results)
readr::write_csv(ki_results, file.path(outDir, "MID_ki_covariate_stats.csv"))
```

```{r raincloud-fn, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
## Raincloud across DRUG (collapsed over reward)
raincloud_drug <- function(data, dv, ylab) {

    geom_rain(

      line.args        = list(colour = "grey", alpha = .5, linewidth = .6),
      point.args       = list(size = 1.5, alpha = .3, shape = 21)

                 linewidth = .9, colour = "black") +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", aes(group = 1),
                 colour = "black", size = 2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = drug_cols) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = drug_cols) +
    labs(x = "Drug", y = ylab) +

}
```

# Ex-Gaussian RT density curves

An ex-Gaussian is fit **per subject** (method of moments) to the
target-locked RTs (hits + lates), each subject's fitted PDF is evaluated on a
common grid and scaled to frequency, and the **group mean +/- SE** is plotted.
Averaging per-subject fits avoids the distortion of fitting one curve to
RTs pooled across subjects.
The ex-Gaussian is defined on positive RTs, so this curve covers hits and lates;
too-early responses (negative target-locked times) are not represented here.

```{r exgauss-fn}
## Ex-Gaussian PDF (mu, sigma, tau)
exg_pdf <- function(x, mu, sigma, tau) {
  (1 / tau) * exp((mu - x) / tau + (sigma^2) / (2 * tau^2)) *
    pnorm((x - mu) / sigma - sigma / tau)
}

## Method-of-moments ex-Gaussian fit (no package needed; this is what
## retimes::mexgauss computes internally).
mexgauss <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x)
  sk <- mean((x - m)^3) / s^3                 # sample skewness
  tau <- s * (abs(sk) / 2)^(1/3)              # tau from third moment
  tau <- max(tau, 1e-4)                       # guard against tau = 0
  mu  <- m - tau
  sigma <- sqrt(max(s^2 - tau^2, 1e-6))       # guard against negative variance
  c(mu = mu, sigma = sigma, tau = tau)
}

## Fit per subject within a group, return group-mean scaled density + SE
exgauss_group <- function(rt_df, grid, bin_width) {
  fits <- rt_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(subject) %>%
    dplyr::filter(sum(!is.na(rt)) >= 10) %>%      # need enough trials to fit
    dplyr::summarise(
      par = list(tryCatch(mexgauss(rt[!is.na(rt)]),
                          error = function(e) c(mu = NA, sigma = NA, tau = NA))),
      n   = sum(!is.na(rt)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  dens <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fits)), function(i) {
    p <- fits$par[[i]]
    if (any(is.na(p))) return(NULL)
    fits$n[i] * exg_pdf(grid, p["mu"], p["sigma"], p["tau"]) * bin_width
  })
  dens <- do.call(rbind, dens[!vapply(dens, is.null, logical(1))])

  data.frame(
    x    = grid,
    mean = colMeans(dens, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = apply(dens, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(dens))
  )
}

## RT data for the curve: hits + lates, target-locked. Uses trial_excl (same
## RT-outlier session exclusion as beh_long), not the unfiltered trial.
rt_curve <- trial_excl %>%
  dplyr::filter(resp %in% c(1, 2), !is.na(rt), rt > 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subject = factor(subject))

grid      <- seq(0, max(rt_curve$rt, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 2000)
bin_width <- diff(range(rt_curve$rt, na.rm = TRUE)) /
             ceiling(sqrt(length(unique(rt_curve$subject))))
```

# Ex-Gaussian parameter statistics (supplementary)

The ex-Gaussian decomposes the RT distribution into a Gaussian component
(`mu`, `sigma`) and an exponential tail (`tau`). `tau` captures occasional slow
responses (lapses), so a drug effect on `tau` specifically would indicate a
change in lapsing rather than a uniform speed shift.

Because per-cell fits (28 trials) are noisy, the Drug and Reward effects are
estimated separately from **collapsed** fits: per subject x drug (56 trials,
collapsed over reward) and per subject x reward (collapsed over drug). This
gives more stable parameter estimates but does not test a Drug x Reward
interaction; the interaction is covered by the RT and categorical analyses.

```{r exgauss-stats}
## Fit ex-Gaussian per subject within each level of a grouping factor.
## Returns one row per subject x level with mu, sigma, tau.
fit_params_by <- function(rt_df, grpvar) {
  rt_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(subject, .data[[grpvar]]) %>%
    dplyr::filter(sum(!is.na(rt)) >= 10) %>%      # enough trials to fit
    dplyr::summarise(
      par = list(tryCatch(mexgauss(rt[!is.na(rt)]),
                          error = function(e) c(mu = NA, sigma = NA, tau = NA))),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      mu    = vapply(par, function(p) p["mu"],    numeric(1)),
      sigma = vapply(par, function(p) p["sigma"], numeric(1)),
      tau   = vapply(par, function(p) p["tau"],   numeric(1))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-par) %>%
    dplyr::rename(level = !!grpvar)
}

## rt_curve (hits + lates, target-locked) is defined in the density section.
params_drug   <- fit_params_by(rt_curve, "drug")
params_reward <- fit_params_by(rt_curve, "reward")

## ---- One-way repeated-measures tests --------------------------------------
## Drug (3 levels): one-way rmANOVA per parameter.
## Reward (2 levels): paired t-test per parameter.
exg_drug_test <- function(param) {
  d <- params_drug %>%
    dplyr::select(subject, level, val = all_of(param)) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  keep <- d %>% dplyr::count(subject) %>% dplyr::filter(n == 3) %>%
    dplyr::pull(subject)
  d <- d %>% dplyr::filter(subject %in% keep) %>% droplevels()

  aov_res <- afex::aov_ez(id = "subject", dv = "val", data = d,
                          within =  "level")  # factor is 'level'
  at <- as.data.frame(aov_res$anova_table)
  data.frame(
    Parameter = param,
    Effect    = "Drug",
    Statistic = sprintf("%.2f (%.0f, %.0f)",
                        at[["F"]], at[["num Df"]], at[["den Df"]]),
    p   = ifelse(at[["Pr(>F)"]] < .001, "< .001",
                 sprintf("%.3f", at[["Pr(>F)"]])),
    ES  = sprintf("%.3f", at[["pes"]]),
    res = I(list(aov_res)),
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE
  )
}

exg_reward_test <- function(param) {
  w <- params_reward %>%
    dplyr::select(subject, level, val = all_of(param)) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = val) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  tt <- t.test(w$Low, w$High, paired = TRUE)
  d  <- unname(tt$statistic) / sqrt(nrow(w))      # Cohen's d, paired
  data.frame(
    Parameter = param,
    Effect    = "Reward",
    Statistic = sprintf("t(%.0f) = %.2f", tt$parameter, tt$statistic),
    p   = ifelse(tt$p.value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", tt$p.value)),
    ES  = sprintf("%.2f", d),
    res = I(list(tt)),
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE
  )
}

params <- c("mu", "sigma", "tau")
exg_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(params, exg_drug_test),
  lapply(params, exg_reward_test)
)

## drop the stored-object column for display, keep ordering Parameter then Effect
exg_tbl <- exg_results %>%
  dplyr::select(-res) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(factor(Parameter, levels = params), Effect)
print(exg_tbl)
```

```{r exgauss-supp-table}
n_per <- exg_tbl %>% dplyr::count(Parameter) %>%

                  tau = "tau (exponential tail)")

        caption = 'Supplementary Table S1. Ex-Gaussian RT parameters: effects of Drug and Reward',
        col.names = c("Effect", "Statistic", "<i>P</i>", "Effect size")) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = "Cambria",
                font_size = 16, position = 'center')

start <- 0
for (i in seq_along(params)) {
  supp_table <- supp_table %>%
    pack_rows(param_labels[params[i]], start + 1, start + n_per[i],
              label_row_css = "font-style: italic;")
  start <- start + n_per[i]
}

  footnote(general = paste(
    "Ex-Gaussian fit by method of moments. Drug effect: one-way",
    "repeated-measures ANOVA (Statistic = F, Effect size = partial eta-squared),",
    "Reward effect: paired t-test",
    "(Statistic = t, Effect size = Cohen's d)."),
    general_title = "Note. ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)

supp_table

  file = file.path(outDir, "MID_exgaussian_table.png"), zoom = 2)
```

# Behavioural drug-effect covariates (for MRI group-level models)

Per-subject MPH-PBO / MPH-SUL / SUL-PBO differences in RT, hit rate,
too-late rate, too-early rate (from `beh_long`) and ex-Gaussian tau (from
`params_drug`), with the same session exclusions as above. Used as
between-subject covariates in the fMRI group models
(`03_group_level/run_groupLevel_vici_MID.m`, `todo.covariate.beh*`) and in
the brain-behaviour scatter plots (`07_brain_behaviour`).

```{r beh-covariates}
## ---- RT / hit / late / early: drug-level means, collapsed over reward ----
beh_drug_lvl <- beh_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subject, drug) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(rt = mean(rt, na.rm = TRUE), hit = mean(hit, na.rm = TRUE),
                   late = mean(late, na.rm = TRUE), early = mean(early, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subject = as.character(subject))

beh_drug_wide <- beh_drug_lvl %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = c(rt, hit, late, early),
                     names_glue = "{.value}{drug}")

## ---- Ex-Gaussian tau: per-subject x drug, same exclusion as above --------
tau_wide <- params_drug %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subject = as.character(subject)) %>%
  dplyr::select(subject, level, tau) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = tau, names_prefix = "tau")

## ---- Deltas ----------------------------------------------------------------
beh_covariates <- beh_drug_wide %>%
  dplyr::full_join(tau_wide, by = "subject") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    subject,
    MPH_PBO_rt    = rtMPH    - rtPBO,    MPH_SUL_rt    = rtMPH    - rtSUL,    SUL_PBO_rt    = rtSUL    - rtPBO,
    MPH_PBO_hit   = hitMPH   - hitPBO,   MPH_SUL_hit   = hitMPH   - hitSUL,   SUL_PBO_hit   = hitSUL   - hitPBO,
    MPH_PBO_late  = lateMPH  - latePBO,  MPH_SUL_late  = lateMPH  - lateSUL,  SUL_PBO_late  = lateSUL  - latePBO,
    MPH_PBO_early = earlyMPH - earlyPBO, MPH_SUL_early = earlyMPH - earlySUL, SUL_PBO_early = earlySUL - earlyPBO,
    MPH_PBO_tau   = tauMPH   - tauPBO,   MPH_SUL_tau   = tauMPH   - tauSUL,   SUL_PBO_tau   = tauSUL   - tauPBO
  )

readr::write_csv(beh_covariates, file.path(outDir, "MID_beh_covariates.csv"))
head(beh_covariates)
```


# Premature (too-early) response-time profile

The ex-Gaussian is defined for positive RTs only, so the curves above
cannot show too-early (pre-target, negative) responses. These are shown
separately here, with the same per-subject-then-average, frequency-scaled
approach (Miller, 1988), but with a nonparametric density per subject
(`stats::density()`). They get their own axis because they are far fewer
than hits and lates, and their shape would be invisible on a shared one.

```{r profile-fn}
## Target-locked response time for ALL responded trials.
## rt is given for hits/lates; for early responses the target-locked time
## is rtCue minus the cue-period duration (raw X15). For hits/lates, where
## both are known, rt equals rtCue - cue_dur.
profile <- raw %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    subject = X1,
    drug    = factor(X4, levels = c(0,1,2), labels = c("PBO","MPH","SUL")),
    reward  = factor(X12, levels = c(1,2), labels = c("Low","High")),
    resp    = X10,
    rt      = X11,
    rtCue   = X13,
    cue_dur = X15           # cue-period duration (target onset rel. to cue)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(reward), resp %in% c(1, 2, -1)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ## hits & lates: rt is already target-locked.
    ## early responses: target-locked time = rtCue - cue_dur (negative).
    rt_target = ifelse(resp == -1, rtCue - cue_dur, rt)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(rt_target)) %>%
  drop_flagged_cells()   # same RT-outlier session exclusion as beh_long/rt_curve

## Per-subject nonparametric density, scaled to frequency and averaged
## (as exgauss_group(), but able to represent negative times). value_col
## selects target-locked (rt_target) or cue-locked (rtCue) times.
full_profile_group <- function(df, grid, bin_width, value_col = "rt_target") {
  fits <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.val = .data[[value_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(subject) %>%
    dplyr::filter(sum(!is.na(.val)) >= 10) %>%      # need enough trials to fit
    dplyr::summarise(
      dens = list(tryCatch(
        stats::density(.val, from = min(grid), to = max(grid), n = length(grid)),
        error = function(e) NULL)),
      n = sum(!is.na(.val)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  dens_mat <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fits)), function(i) {
    d <- fits$dens[[i]]
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    fits$n[i] * d$y * bin_width
  })
  dens_mat <- do.call(rbind, dens_mat[!vapply(dens_mat, is.null, logical(1))])

  data.frame(
    x    = grid,
    mean = colMeans(dens_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = apply(dens_mat, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(dens_mat))
  )
}

## Premature (resp == -1) trials only. rt_target can be as early as
## -cue_dur (the cue period is 3-6 s), hence the -6 to 0 s window.
premature <- profile %>% dplyr::filter(resp == -1)

grid_premature      <- seq(-6, 0, length.out = 2000)
bin_width_premature <- diff(range(premature$rt_target, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                        ceiling(sqrt(length(unique(premature$subject))))

## Raw cue-locked time (rtCue), NOT adjusted for cue_dur: a diagnostic
## companion to the rt_target plots. rtCue >= 0 for every response type.
grid_rtCue      <- seq(0, 8, length.out = 2000)
bin_width_rtCue <- diff(range(profile$rtCue, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                   ceiling(sqrt(length(unique(profile$subject))))
```

```{r profile-drug, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
dens_premature_drug <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(levels(premature$drug), function(dr) {
  full_profile_group(dplyr::filter(premature, drug == dr), grid_premature, bin_width_premature) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(drug = dr)
})) %>% dplyr::mutate(drug = factor(drug, levels = c("PBO", "MPH", "SUL")))

p_profile_drug <- ggplot(dens_premature_drug, aes(x, mean, colour = drug, fill = drug)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - se, 0), ymax = mean + se), alpha = .2, colour = NA) +
  ## semi-transparent lines, so overlapping curves stay visible
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = .7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = drug_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = drug_cols) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Response time relative to target onset (s)",
       y = "Frequency", colour = "Drug", fill = "Drug",
       subtitle = "Premature (too-early) responses only") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

save_fig(p_profile_drug, "premature_rt_drug", width = 6, height = 4)
p_profile_drug
```

```{r profile-reward, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
dens_premature_reward <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(levels(premature$reward), function(rw) {
  full_profile_group(dplyr::filter(premature, reward == rw), grid_premature, bin_width_premature) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(reward = rw)
})) %>% dplyr::mutate(reward = factor(reward, levels = c("Low", "High")))

save_fig(p_profile_reward, "premature_rt_reward", width = 6, height = 4)
p_profile_reward
```

## Raw cue-locked time (diagnostic, not target-locked)

`rtCue` without the `cue_dur` adjustment. Because the cue period is
jittered (3-6 s), a hit/late response's `rtCue` is `cue_dur + rt`, so the
hit/late peak is smeared here compared with the target-locked plots. A
sanity check on those plots, not a replacement (not evaluated by default).

```{r profile-rtcue-drug, eval=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, include=FALSE}
dens_rtCue_drug <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(levels(profile$drug), function(dr) {
  full_profile_group(dplyr::filter(profile, drug == dr), grid_rtCue, bin_width_rtCue,
                     value_col = "rtCue") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(drug = dr)
})) %>% dplyr::mutate(drug = factor(drug, levels = c("PBO", "MPH", "SUL")))

p_rtcue_drug <- ggplot(dens_rtCue_drug, aes(x, mean, colour = drug, fill = drug)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), alpha = .2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = .7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = drug_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = drug_cols) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 8)) +
  labs(x = "Response time relative to cue onset (s), uncorrected for cue duration",
       y = "Frequency", colour = "Drug", fill = "Drug") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

save_fig(p_rtcue_drug, "rtCue_raw_drug", width = 6, height = 4)
p_rtcue_drug
```

# Neural cluster tables (whole-brain TFCE)

Publication tables of the whole-brain TFCE-corrected clusters, built from
`all_clusters_<hrf_type>.csv` and `all_regions_<hrf_type>.csv`
(`05_cluster_tables/combine_cluster_tables.m`). Run this section after the
fMRI pipeline; the rest of the document does not depend on it.

- **Task activation** (session average): reported per anatomical region
  rather than as a peak list, because TFCE yields very large clusters that
  a few peak coordinates describe poorly.
- **Drug effects** (MPH vs PBO / MPH vs SUL / SUL vs PBO).
- **Behavioural covariate effects** (individual behavioural drug effect as
  a covariate on the matching drug comparison).

```{r neural-cluster-load}
neural_hrf_type <- "canonical_hrf"   # must match what combine_cluster_tables.m was run with

neural_clusters_file <- file.path(projectDir, "bids", "derivatives", "mri",
                                  "groupLevel", "MID", "regular", neural_hrf_type,
                                  sprintf("all_clusters_%s.csv", neural_hrf_type))

clusters_raw <- readr::read_csv(neural_clusters_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  ## readr reads empty fields as NA; the no-covariate rows need ""
  dplyr::mutate(Covariate = tidyr::replace_na(Covariate, ""))

## Per-region breakdown of the same clusters: one row per cluster x region
neural_regions_file <- file.path(projectDir, "bids", "derivatives", "mri",
                                 "groupLevel", "MID", "regular", neural_hrf_type,
                                 sprintf("all_regions_%s.csv", neural_hrf_type))

regions_raw <- readr::read_csv(neural_regions_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Covariate = tidyr::replace_na(Covariate, ""))
```

```{r neural-cluster-labels}
## Analyses to report. Like contrast_labels below, this also filters: rows
## not listed (e.g. the single-drug models "MPH"/"PBO"/"SUL") are dropped.
drug_labels <- c(
  sessionAverage = "Session average",
  MPHvsPBO       = "MPH vs PBO",
  MPHvsSUL       = "MPH vs SUL",
  SULvsPBO       = "SUL vs PBO"
)

## Task contrasts to report, in table order; contrasts not listed are
## dropped from every table.
contrast_labels <- c(
  Cue       = "Anticipation (across reward)",
  HCvsLC    = "High vs low reward cue",
  HitvsMiss = "Hit vs miss",
  Target    = "Target"
)

## Covariate stem -> readable label, e.g. "ki_wholeStriatum" -> "Ki (whole striatum)"
covariate_label <- function(covariate) {
  map <- c(ki_VS_new = "Ventral striatum ki", ki_wholeStriatum = "Whole striatum ki",
           ki_wholeCaudate = "Caudate ki", ki_wholePutamen = "Putamen ki",
           ## behavioural drug-effect covariates
           mphBehEffect_hit    = "MPH hit-rate benefit",
           mphBehEffect_early  = "MPH premature-response change",
           mphBehEffect_late   = "MPH late-response change",
           mphBehEffect_rt     = "MPH reaction-time change",
           tauEffect_MPHvsPBO  = "MPH tau change",
           hitEffect_MPHvsSUL  = "MPH-vs-SUL hit-rate difference",
           lateEffect_MPHvsSUL = "MPH-vs-SUL late-response difference",
           rtEffect_MPHvsSUL   = "MPH-vs-SUL reaction-time difference",
           TauEffect_MPHvsSUL  = "MPH-vs-SUL tau difference",
           SULvsPBO_late       = "SUL late-response change")
  out <- ifelse(covariate == "", "", unname(map[covariate]))
  ifelse(is.na(out) & covariate != "", covariate, out)   # fall back to the raw stem if unmapped
}

hemi_labels <- c(L = "Left", R = "Right", M = "Midline")

## Optional renaming of atlas regions in the tables (name = label as in the
## CSV, value = printed label). Example:
##   region_rename <- c("POrG posterior orbital gyrus"  = "OFC",
##                      "ACgG anterior cingulate gyrus" = "ACC",
##                      "PCgG posterior cingulate gyrus" = "PCC")
region_rename <- character(0)
apply_region_rename <- function(region) {
  if (length(region_rename) == 0) return(region)
  hit <- region %in% names(region_rename)
  region[hit] <- unname(region_rename[region[hit]])
  region
}

clusters_tbl <- clusters_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(TaskContrast %in% names(contrast_labels),
                DrugComparison %in% names(drug_labels)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Region = apply_region_rename(Region),
    DrugLabel = dplyr::coalesce(unname(drug_labels[DrugComparison]), DrugComparison),
    CovLabel  = covariate_label(Covariate),
    Model     = ifelse(CovLabel == "", DrugLabel, paste0(DrugLabel, " × ", CovLabel)),
    Contrast_label = dplyr::coalesce(unname(contrast_labels[TaskContrast]), TaskContrast),
    Direction_label = ifelse(Direction == "positive", "Positive", "Negative"),
    Hemisphere_label = dplyr::coalesce(unname(hemi_labels[Hemisphere]), Hemisphere),
    Coordinates = sprintf("%d, %d, %d", round(x), round(y), round(z)),
    Peak_t_fmt  = sprintf("%.2f", Peak_t),
    p_fmt       = ifelse(pFWE < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", pFWE))
  )

## Same labelling for the region breakdown, plus its own display columns.
regions_tbl <- regions_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(TaskContrast %in% names(contrast_labels),
                DrugComparison %in% names(drug_labels)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Region = apply_region_rename(Region),
    DrugLabel = dplyr::coalesce(unname(drug_labels[DrugComparison]), DrugComparison),
    CovLabel  = covariate_label(Covariate),
    Model     = ifelse(CovLabel == "", DrugLabel, paste0(DrugLabel, " × ", CovLabel)),
    Contrast_label   = dplyr::coalesce(unname(contrast_labels[TaskContrast]), TaskContrast),
    Direction_label  = factor(ifelse(Direction == "positive", "Positive", "Negative"),
                              levels = c("Positive", "Negative")),
    Hemisphere_label = dplyr::coalesce(unname(hemi_labels[Hemisphere]), Hemisphere),
    Coordinates   = sprintf("%d, %d, %d", round(x), round(y), round(z)),
    Peak_t_fmt    = sprintf("%.2f", Peak_t),
    p_fmt         = ifelse(pFWE < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", pFWE)),
    Cluster_label = sprintf("%d (k = %s)", Cluster,
                            format(Size_k, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
    Region_k_fmt   = format(Region_k, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
    Region_pct_fmt = sprintf("%.1f", Region_pct)
  )

## White matter and ventricles make up a large share of the big clusters
## without being anatomically informative; they are left out of the region
## tables (noted in the footnote). character(0) keeps them.
region_exclude <- c("Cerebral White Matter", "Lateral Ventricle")

## Fixed order for the non-covariate models, covariate combinations appended
## afterwards in whatever order they first appear.
model_levels <- c(unname(drug_labels))
extra_levels <- setdiff(unique(clusters_tbl$Model), model_levels)
model_levels <- c(model_levels[model_levels %in% clusters_tbl$Model], extra_levels)

clusters_tbl <- clusters_tbl %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = model_levels)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Model, factor(Contrast_label, levels = unname(contrast_labels)),
                 dplyr::desc(Size_k))
```

```{r neural-cluster-table-fn}
## Builds, prints, and saves (csv/png/pdf) one cluster table from a subset of
## clusters_tbl, grouped/packed by whichever column name is passed as
## group_var ("Model" or "Contrast_label"). group_levels fixes the row-group
## order; must cover every value of group_var actually present in `data`.
if (!requireNamespace("webshot2", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("webshot2")

## bonferroni_n: when given, adds a column of pFWE multiplied by that number,
## capped at 1. TFCE controls the family-wise error rate WITHIN one map but
## not across the number of maps tested, so the covariate tables carry this
## second correction; leave NULL for the pre-planned contrasts, which are not
## corrected across the cells of the design.
build_cluster_table <- function(data, group_var, group_levels, caption, basename,
                                bonferroni_n = NULL) {
  disp <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(GroupVar = factor(.data[[group_var]], levels = group_levels)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(GroupVar, factor(Contrast_label, levels = unname(contrast_labels)),
                   dplyr::desc(Size_k)) %>%
    {if (is.null(bonferroni_n)) . else dplyr::mutate(., p_bonf_fmt = {
       pb <- pmin(1, pFWE * bonferroni_n)
       ifelse(pb < .001, "&lt; .001", sprintf("%.3f", pb))
     })} %>%
    dplyr::select(GroupVar, Contrast_label, Direction_label, Region, Hemisphere_label,
                  Coordinates, Peak_t_fmt, Size_k, p_fmt,
                  dplyr::any_of("p_bonf_fmt"))

  group_counts <- disp %>% dplyr::count(GroupVar) %>% dplyr::arrange(GroupVar)

  tbl <- disp %>%
    dplyr::select(-GroupVar) %>%
    kable("html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, caption = caption,
          col.names = c("Contrast", "Direction", "Region", "Hemisphere",
                        "MNI (x, y, z)", "Peak t", "k", "<i>P</i>FWE",
                        if (is.null(bonferroni_n)) NULL else "<i>P</i>Bonf")) %>%
    kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = "Cambria",
                  font_size = 14, position = "center") %>%
    ## Keep coordinates and contrast labels on one line
    kableExtra::column_spec(1, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;",
                            include_thead = TRUE) %>%
    kableExtra::column_spec(5, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;",
                            include_thead = TRUE)

  start <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(group_counts$GroupVar)) {
    tbl <- tbl %>%
      pack_rows(as.character(group_counts$GroupVar[i]), start + 1,
                start + group_counts$n[i],
                label_row_css = "font-style: italic; background-color: #f2f2f2;")
    start <- start + group_counts$n[i]
  }

  tbl <- tbl %>%
    footnote(general = paste(
      "All clusters survive threshold-free cluster enhancement (TFCE),",
      "family-wise-error corrected at p < .05. Direction is 'Positive' for",
      "the first-named condition/drug (or higher covariate values) showing",
      "greater activation, 'Negative' for the reverse -- see Methods for the",
      "exact contrast definitions. k = cluster size in voxels.",
      if (is.null(bonferroni_n)) "" else paste(
        "<i>P</i>Bonf is <i>P</i>FWE multiplied by", bonferroni_n,
        "and capped at 1, correcting for the number of covariate maps tested",
        "in addition to the within-map TFCE correction.")),
      general_title = "Note. ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE, escape = FALSE)

  readr::write_csv(data, file.path(outDir, paste0(basename, ".csv")))
  kableExtra::save_kable(tbl, file = file.path(outDir, paste0(basename, ".png")), zoom = 2)
  kableExtra::save_kable(tbl, file = file.path(outDir, paste0(basename, ".pdf")))

  tbl
}

## Same for the per-region breakdown (different columns: regions, not peaks)
build_region_table <- function(data, group_levels, caption, basename) {
  disp_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!Region %in% region_exclude) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(GroupVar = factor(Contrast_label, levels = group_levels)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(GroupVar, Direction_label, dplyr::desc(Size_k),
                   dplyr::desc(Region_k))

  disp <- disp_data %>%
    dplyr::select(GroupVar, Direction_label, Cluster_label, Region, Hemisphere_label,
                  Region_k_fmt, Region_pct_fmt, Coordinates, Peak_t_fmt, p_fmt)

  group_counts <- disp %>% dplyr::count(GroupVar) %>% dplyr::arrange(GroupVar)

  tbl <- disp %>%
    dplyr::select(-GroupVar) %>%
    kable("html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, caption = caption,
          col.names = c("Direction", "Cluster", "Region", "Hemisphere",
                        "Voxels", "% of cluster", "MNI (x, y, z)", "Peak t",
                        "<i>P</i>FWE")) %>%
    kable_classic(full_width = FALSE, html_font = "Cambria",
                  font_size = 14, position = "center") %>%
    ## Keep coordinates on one line
    kableExtra::column_spec(7, extra_css = "white-space: nowrap;",
                            include_thead = TRUE)

  start <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(group_counts$GroupVar)) {
    tbl <- tbl %>%
      pack_rows(as.character(group_counts$GroupVar[i]), start + 1,
                start + group_counts$n[i],
                label_row_css = "font-style: italic; background-color: #f2f2f2;")
    start <- start + group_counts$n[i]
  }

  tbl <- tbl %>%
    footnote(general = paste(
      "All clusters survive threshold-free cluster enhancement (TFCE),",
      "family-wise-error corrected at p < .05. Each row is one anatomical",
      "region (Neuromorphometrics atlas) within one cluster: Voxels is the",
      "number of that cluster's significant voxels falling in the region,",
      "'% of cluster' their share of it, and the coordinates and peak t are",
      "the strongest voxel within that region. Clusters are listed as",
      "'cluster number (k = total voxels)'. Because TFCE returns very large",
      "contiguous clusters, spatial specificity is limited and a cluster",
      "should not be read as evidence for any single region within it",
      "(Woo et al., 2014). White-matter and ventricle labels are omitted.",
      "Direction is 'Positive' for the first-named condition showing greater",
      "activation, 'Negative' for the reverse."),
      general_title = "Note. ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)

  readr::write_csv(disp_data, file.path(outDir, paste0(basename, ".csv")))
  kableExtra::save_kable(tbl, file = file.path(outDir, paste0(basename, ".png")), zoom = 2)
  kableExtra::save_kable(tbl, file = file.path(outDir, paste0(basename, ".pdf")))

  tbl
}
```

## Task activation (supplementary)

```{r neural-cluster-task}
avg_task_regions <- regions_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(Covariate == "", DrugComparison == "sessionAverage")

build_region_table(
  avg_task_regions, unname(contrast_labels),
  paste("Supplementary Table S3. Whole-brain TFCE-corrected clusters:",
        "task activation (session average), broken down by",
        "anatomical region"),
  "MID_neural_clusters_task_activation"
)
```

## Drug effects (main text)

```{r neural-cluster-drug}
drug_tbl <- clusters_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(Covariate == "", DrugComparison != "sessionAverage")

build_cluster_table(
  drug_tbl, "Model", model_levels[model_levels %in% unique(drug_tbl$Model)],
  paste("Table 2. Whole-brain TFCE-corrected clusters: drug effects on",
        "task-related activation"),
  "MID_neural_clusters_drug_effects"
)
```

## ki covariate effects

Not tabled here; the ki covariate results are reported in the text. A
table can be built the same way, filtering on
`startsWith(Covariate, "ki_")`.

## Behavioural covariate effects (supplementary)

```{r neural-cluster-behcov}
behcov_tbl <- clusters_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(Covariate != "", !startsWith(as.character(Covariate), "ki_"))

if (nrow(behcov_tbl) == 0) {
  message("No behavioural covariate clusters to table.")
} else {
  build_cluster_table(
    behcov_tbl, "Model",
    model_levels[model_levels %in% unique(behcov_tbl$Model)],
    paste("Supplementary Table S4. Whole-brain TFCE-corrected clusters:",
          "individual differences in the behavioural drug effect as a",
          "covariate on the corresponding drug comparison"),
    "MID_neural_clusters_beh_covariates",
    bonferroni_n = 88   # number of behavioural-covariate maps tested
  )
}
```
